module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Grimm's conjecture

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grimm%27s_conjecture)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Function

namespace Grimm

/--
**Grimm's Conjecture**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then there are $k$ distinct primes $p_i$
such that $p_i$ divides $n + i$ for all $0 \le i \le k-1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem grimm_conjecture (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin k, (n + i).Composite) :
    ∃ ps : Fin k ↪ ℕ,  ∀ i : Fin k, (ps i).Prime ∧ ps i ∣ (n + i) := by
  sorry

/--
**Grimm's Conjecture, weaker version**
If $n, n+1, \dots, n+k-1$ are all composite numbers, then their product
has at least $k$ distinct prime divisors.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem grimm_conjecture_weak (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 1 ≤ k)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin k, (n + i).Composite) :
    ∃ ps : Fin k ↪ ℕ,  ∀ i : Fin k, (ps i).Prime ∧ ∃ j : Fin k, ps i ∣ (n + j) := by
  sorry

end Grimm

reformulations.difference: Instead of counting distinct prime divisors of the product, Lean requests an embedding of Fin k into the primes, each of whose values divides some term of the interval.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The product is nonzero because n ≥ 1. A prime divides this finite product exactly when it divides one of its terms. Thus the requested embedding exists exactly when the product has at least k distinct prime divisors. Reindexing the starting point converts n,…,n+k−1 to the source's m+1,…,m+k; compositeness of the first term guarantees m=n−1≥1. On the source's domain, having no prime in the interval is equivalent to all its terms being composite. GrimmReview.weak_source_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean proves the full equivalence using the actual declaration's type, without sorryAx.

https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0765 — Shanta Laishram and M. Ram Murty, Grimm's Conjecture and Smooth Numbers, Michigan Mathematical Journal 61 (2012), 151–160.

review.notes: Both declarations faithfully state their respective conjectures. The source still records both as unproven, consistent with the research open tags. Confirmed that Nat.Composite excludes 0 and 1 and that the embeddings enforce distinctness. The scratch file compiles and checks the harmless index shift, empty and singleton cases, and an explicit prime assignment for 8,9,10. A finite search over n<200 and k<14 found no failures. The reviewed repository file was not modified.
